authoredSolutions.1: Young's modulus is \(Y=\dfrac{\text{stress}}{\text{longitudinal strain}}\). Raising the temperature increases the mean interatomic separation and weakens the interatomic bonding, so the same applied stress produces a larger strain. Hence \(Y\) falls steadily with temperature (it does not vary erratically, and it certainly does not stay fixed). The correct choice is B, decreases.
authoredSolutions.2: At height \(h=2R\) the distance from the centre is \(3R\), so \[g'=\frac{GM}{(3R)^{2}}=\frac{g}{9}=\frac{\pi^{2}}{9}\ m/s^{2}.\] A second's pendulum has time period \(T=2\ s\), and \(T=2\pi\sqrt{l/g'}\), so \[2=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{l}{g'}}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\pi^{2}}=\frac{l}{g'}\Rightarrow l=\frac{g'}{\pi^{2}}=\frac{\pi^{2}/9}{\pi^{2}}=\frac{1}{9}\ m.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.3: From the figure \(V_{s}=8\ V\), \(V_{z}=5\ V\) and \(R_{L}=1\ k\Omega\). The load draws \[I_{L}=\frac{5}{1000}=5\ mA,\] and the Zener can carry at most \[I_{z,\max}=\frac{P}{V_{z}}=\frac{10\ mW}{5\ V}=2\ mA.\] The drop across the series resistor is \(8-5=3\ V\). The series current lies between \(5\ mA\) (Zener just conducting) and \(5+2=7\ mA\), so \[\frac{3}{7\times10^{-3}}\ \Omega\le R_{s}\le\frac{3}{5\times10^{-3}}\ \Omega,\quad\text{i.e.}\quad 429\ \Omega\le R_{s}\le 600\ \Omega.\] None of \(5\ k\Omega\), \(10\ \Omega\) or \(1\ k\Omega\) lies in this window, so the correct choice is D, none of these.
authoredSolutions.4: The figure shows eight identical cells, each of emf \(5\ V\) and internal resistance \(0.2\ \Omega\), all driving the same single loop, with the ideal voltmeter connected across one of them. The loop current is \[I=\frac{8\times 5}{8\times 0.2}=\frac{40}{1.6}=25\ A.\] The voltmeter reads the terminal potential difference of the cell it spans, \[V=E-Ir=5-25\times0.2=0\ V.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.5: Joining like plates puts the capacitors in parallel with total charge \(CV+2CV=3CV\) on total capacitance \(2C\), so the common potential is \[V_{f}=\frac{3CV}{2C}=\frac{3V}{2}.\] Initial energy \[U_{i}=\tfrac12 CV^{2}+\tfrac12 C(2V)^{2}=\tfrac52 CV^{2},\] final energy \[U_{f}=\tfrac12(2C)\left(\tfrac{3V}{2}\right)^{2}=\tfrac94 CV^{2}.\] The decrease is \(U_{i}-U_{f}=\left(\tfrac52-\tfrac94\right)CV^{2}=\tfrac14 CV^{2}\). The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.6: For a mixture, \[C_{V}=\frac{n_{1}C_{V_{1}}+n_{2}C_{V_{2}}}{n_{1}+n_{2}}.\] With \(n_{1}=2\) moles monoatomic \(\left(C_{V}=\tfrac32R\right)\) and \(n_{2}=6\) moles diatomic \(\left(C_{V}=\tfrac52R\right)\), \[C_{V}=\frac{2\left(\tfrac32R\right)+6\left(\tfrac52R\right)}{8}=\frac{3R+15R}{8}=\frac{9}{4}R.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.7: For a horizontal circle the string tension supplies the centripetal force, \(T=m\omega^{2}l\). At the breaking limit \[400=0.5\times\omega^{2}\times0.5\Rightarrow \omega^{2}=1600\Rightarrow\omega=40\ rad/s.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.8: The rms conduction current is \[I=\frac{V}{X_{C}}=V\omega C=230\times300\times200\times10^{-12}=1.38\times10^{-5}\ A=13.8\ \mu A.\] Maxwell's correction requires the displacement current between the plates to equal the conduction current in the leads at every instant, so it is also \(13.8\ \mu A\). The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.9: For a polytropic process \(PV^{n}=\) constant the work done by the gas is \[W=\frac{P_{1}V_{1}-P_{2}V_{2}}{n-1}.\] Here \(n=\tfrac32\), so \(n-1=\tfrac12\) and \[W=2\left(P_{1}V_{1}-P_{2}V_{2}\right).\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.10: A series multiplier \(R\) must drop the excess voltage at full-scale current \(I_{g}=5\ mA\): \[R=\frac{V}{I_{g}}-G=\frac{100}{5\times10^{-3}}-50=20000-50=19950\ \Omega.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.11: From \(\lambda=\dfrac{h}{mv}\) we get \(v=\dfrac{h}{m\lambda}\), so \[\frac{v_{p}}{v_{\alpha}}=\frac{m_{\alpha}}{m_{p}}\times\frac{\lambda_{\alpha}}{\lambda_{p}}=4\times\frac{2\lambda}{\lambda}=8.\] The ratio is \(8:1\); the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.12: Given \(10\ MSD=11\ VSD\), so \(1\ VSD=\tfrac{10}{11}\ MSD\). The least count is \[LC=1\ MSD-1\ VSD=\left(1-\frac{10}{11}\right)MSD=\frac{1}{11}MSD=\frac{5}{11}\ \text{units}.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.13: Resonance requires \(\omega_{0}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\) to be unchanged, so \(L'C'=LC\). With \(C'=4C\), \[L'(4C)=LC\Rightarrow L'=\frac{L}{4}.\] The inductance must therefore be reduced by \(L-\tfrac{L}{4}=\tfrac34L\). The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.14: Since \(\rho=\dfrac{R\pi r^{2}}{l}\), \[\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}=\frac{\Delta R}{R}+2\frac{\Delta r}{r}+\frac{\Delta l}{l}=\frac{10}{100}+2\times\frac{0.05}{0.35}+\frac{0.2}{15}.\] This gives \(0.100+0.2857+0.0133=0.399\), i.e. \(39.9\%\). The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.15: Angular impulse equals the change in angular momentum, and angular momentum has the dimensions of \(mvr\): \[[L]=[M][LT^{-1}][L]=\left[ML^{2}T^{-1}\right].\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.16: The bullet embeds, so momentum is conserved in the perfectly inelastic collision: \[mu=(M+m)V\Rightarrow 10^{-2}\times2\times10^{2}=(1+10^{-2})V\Rightarrow V\approx 2\ m/s.\] Afterwards mechanical energy is conserved as the bob swings up: \[h=\frac{V^{2}}{2g}=\frac{4}{20}=0.20\ m.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.17: The circular speed is \(v=\dfrac{2\pi R}{T}\). For projection at angle \(\theta\), \[H=\frac{v^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}=4R\Rightarrow \frac{4\pi^{2}R^{2}}{T^{2}}\cdot\frac{\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}=4R.\] Hence \[\sin^{2}\theta=\frac{2gT^{2}}{\pi^{2}R}\Rightarrow \theta=\sin^{-1}\left[\frac{2gT^{2}}{\pi^{2}R}\right]^{1/2}.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.18: The figure gives a trolley of mass \(20\ kg\) on the table and a hanging block of weight \(60\ N\) (mass \(6\ kg\)). Kinetic friction on the trolley is \[f_{k}=\mu N=0.04\times20\times10=8\ N.\] For the connected system, \[a=\frac{60-8}{20+6}=\frac{52}{26}=2\ ms^{-2}.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.19: Balmer emission ends on \(n=2\), so the atom must first be excited to at least \(n=3\). The energy needed from the ground state is \[\Delta E=13.6\left(\frac{1}{1^{2}}-\frac{1}{3^{2}}\right)=13.6\times\frac{8}{9}\approx 12.1\ eV.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.20: With the pattern formed in the focal plane of a lens of focal length \(f\), the linear width of the central maximum is \[W=\frac{2\lambda f}{a}=\frac{2\times6\times10^{-7}\times0.2}{1\times10^{-5}}=2.4\times10^{-2}\ m=24\ mm.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.21: Each side of the hexagon has length \(a=\dfrac{4\pi}{6}=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\ m\), and the perpendicular distance from the centre to a side is \[r=\frac{a}{2}\cot 30^{\circ}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\cdot\sqrt3=\frac{a\sqrt3}{2}=\frac{\pi\sqrt3}{3}=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt3}\ m.\] Each finite side subtends \(30^{\circ}\) on either side of the foot of the perpendicular, so \[B=6\times\frac{\mu_{0}I}{4\pi r}\left(\sin 30^{\circ}+\sin 30^{\circ}\right)=6\times\frac{10^{-7}\times 4\pi\sqrt3}{\pi/\sqrt3}=6\times 12\times10^{-7}=72\times10^{-7}\ T.\] Hence \(x=72\).
authoredSolutions.22: The spatial gradient is \(\left|\dfrac{dB}{dx}\right|=10^{-3}\ T/cm=0.1\ T/m\), so across the \(12\ cm\) separation of the two vertical arms the fields differ by \(0.1\times0.12=1.2\times10^{-2}\ T\). The motional contribution is \[\varepsilon_{1}=\left(\Delta B\right)lv=1.2\times10^{-2}\times0.05\times0.05=3\times10^{-5}\ V=300\times10^{-7}\ V.\] The time variation contributes \[\varepsilon_{2}=A\left|\frac{dB}{dt}\right|=\left(0.12\times0.05\right)\times10^{-3}=6\times10^{-6}\ V=60\times10^{-7}\ V.\] These add to \(\varepsilon=360\times10^{-7}\ V\), so \[P=\frac{\varepsilon^{2}}{R}=\frac{\left(3.6\times10^{-5}\right)^{2}}{6\times10^{-3}}=2.16\times10^{-7}\ W=216\times10^{-9}\ W.\] Hence the answer is 216.
authoredSolutions.23: For a virtual erect image of a convex lens, \(m=+3\) gives \(v=3u\) with both on the same side. Taking \(u=-u_{0}\), \(v=-3u_{0}\), the separation is \[|v|-|u|=3u_{0}-u_{0}=2u_{0}=20\ cm\Rightarrow u_{0}=10\ cm.\] Then \[\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{-30}-\frac{1}{-10}=\frac{-1+3}{30}=\frac{1}{15},\] so \(f=15\ cm\).
authoredSolutions.24: For each suspended sphere, \(\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}=\dfrac{F}{W}\). In water the Coulomb force falls by the dielectric constant \(K\), while the effective weight falls by buoyancy: \[W'=W\left(1-\frac{\rho_{w}}{\rho_{s}}\right)=W\left(1-\frac{1}{1.5}\right)=\frac{W}{3}.\] Equal angles require \[\frac{F}{W}=\frac{F/K}{W/3}\Rightarrow 1=\frac{3}{K}\Rightarrow K=3.\]
authoredSolutions.26: Place the right-angle vertex at the origin with the other two spheres at \(4\hat{i}\) and \(4\hat{j}\). authoredSolutions.27: For a stretched wire \(f=\dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}\propto\sqrt{T}\). At \(6\ N\) the wire resonates with the fork, so \(f_{\text{fork}}=f_{1}\). At \(54\ N\), \[f_{2}=f_{1}\sqrt{\frac{54}{6}}=3f_{1}.\] The beat frequency gives \[f_{2}-f_{1}=2f_{1}=12\Rightarrow f_{1}=6\ Hz.\] The frequency of the tuning fork is \(6\ Hz\).
authoredSolutions.28: Convert the speeds: \(180\ km/h=50\ m/s\) below and \(252\ km/h=70\ m/s\) above. Bernoulli's theorem gives the pressure difference \[\Delta P=\frac{1}{2}\rho\left(v_{\text{upper}}^{2}-v_{\text{lower}}^{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\times1\times\left(70^{2}-50^{2}\right)=1200\ Pa.\] The total wing area is \(2\times40=80\ m^{2}\), so in level flight \[mg=\Delta P\times A=1200\times80=96000\ N\Rightarrow m=\frac{96000}{10}=9600\ kg.\]

authoredSolutions.90: \(R_1-R_2\) consists of pairs with \(a\mid b\) and \(a\ne b\). Count \(=\sum_a(\lfloor20/a\rfloor-1)=19+9+5+4+3+2+1+1+1+1=46\).
authoredSolutions.91: With \(5\%\) of the current through the galvanometer, \(I_{g}=0.05I\) and the shunt carries \(I_{s}=0.95I\). Equal potential differences give \[0.05I\,G=0.95I\,S\Rightarrow S=\frac{G}{19}.\] The ammeter resistance is the parallel combination, \[R_{A}=\frac{SG}{S+G}=\frac{G^{2}/19}{20G/19}=\frac{G}{20}.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.92: The figure is a Wheatstone bridge with \(AB=0.8\ m\Omega\), \(AD=1\ m\Omega\), \(DC=3\ m\Omega\) and the semiconductor in \(BC\). Null deflection requires \[\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{AD}{DC}\Rightarrow \frac{0.8}{R}=\frac{1}{3}\Rightarrow R=2.4\ m\Omega.\] Cooling at \(2\ ^{\circ}C/s\) for \(10\ s\) is a change of \(20\ ^{\circ}C\), while the resistance changes by \(\Delta R=2.4-3=-0.6\ m\Omega\). Hence \[|\alpha|=\frac{|\Delta R|}{R\,\Delta T}=\frac{0.6}{3\times20}=1\times10^{-2}\ ^{\circ}C^{-1},\] and for a semiconductor the coefficient is taken negative, \(\alpha=-1\times10^{-2}\ ^{\circ}C^{-1}\). The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.93: Statement (B) is true: the nuclear force is short-ranged and does not follow an inverse square law. Statement (C) is true: the nucleon-nucleon force depends on the relative spin orientation. Statement (E) is true: a smaller packing fraction corresponds to greater stability. Statement (D) is false, because a spin-dependent force has a non-central (tensor) part, even though it is charge independent. Statement (A) is Bohr's quantisation postulate, which the paper intends as correct. The set (A), (B), (C), (E) is therefore the intended answer, so the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.94: From \(\gamma=1+\dfrac{2}{f}=1.4\) we get \(f=5\). For an isobaric process \(W=nR\Delta T=200\ J\) and \[Q=nC_{P}\Delta T=n\left(\frac{f+2}{2}\right)R\Delta T=\frac{7}{2}\times200=700\ J.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.95: The incline is smooth, so no friction torque acts on the disc and its angular speed, hence its rotational kinetic energy, is unchanged as it rises. Only the translational kinetic energy converts to potential energy: \[\frac{1}{2}Mv^{2}=Mgh\Rightarrow h=\frac{v^{2}}{2g}=\frac{1}{2}\frac{v^{2}}{g}.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.96: The threshold wavelength corresponds to the band gap: \[E_{g}=\frac{hc}{\lambda}=\frac{6.6\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^{8}}{660\times10^{-9}\times1.6\times10^{-19}}\ eV=\frac{1.98\times10^{-25}}{1.056\times10^{-25}}=1.875\ eV=\frac{15}{8}\ eV.\] So \(X=15\) and the correct choice is A.

authoredSolutions.98: In air the wave travels at \(c\), so \[\lambda=\frac{c}{f}=\frac{3\times10^{8}}{60\times10^{6}}=5\ m.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.99: By the impulse-momentum theorem the average force is the rate of change of momentum: \[F=\frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}=\frac{0.120\times25}{0.1}=30\ N.\] By Newton's third law the ball exerts the same magnitude on the hand, so the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.100: Each photon carries energy \(hf\), so the emission rate is \[n=\frac{P}{hf}=\frac{2\times10^{-3}}{6.63\times10^{-34}\times6\times10^{14}}=\frac{2\times10^{-3}}{3.978\times10^{-19}}\approx5\times10^{15}\ s^{-1}.\] The correct choice is C.

authoredSolutions.103: Since \(v_{rms}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}\propto\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}\) at fixed temperature, \[\frac{v_{H_{2}}}{v_{O_{2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{32}{2}}=4\Rightarrow v_{O_{2}}=\frac{2}{4}=0.5\ km/s.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.104: Take north as positive: \(v_{A}=72\ km/h=+20\ ms^{-1}\) and \(v_{B}=108\ km/h\) south \(=-30\ ms^{-1}\). Then \[v_{B/A}=v_{B}-v_{A}=-30-20=-50\ ms^{-1},\] \[v_{G/B}=0-v_{B}=+30\ ms^{-1}.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.105: In the steady state no current flows through the capacitor arms, so the \(6\ V\) source drives current through \(4\ \Omega\), the galvanometer \(2\ \Omega\) and \(6\ \Omega\) in series: \[I=\frac{6}{4+2+6}=0.5\ A.\] Taking the negative terminal as zero, the potentials give a drop of \(0.5\times4=2\ V\) across the \(4\ \Omega\) arm and \(0.5\times2=1\ V\) across the galvanometer, so \[V_{C_{1}}=3\ V,\qquad V_{C_{2}}=4\ V.\] Hence \(q_{1}=4\times3=12\ \mu C\), \(q_{2}=6\times4=24\ \mu C\) and \[\frac{q_{1}}{q_{2}}=\frac{1}{2}.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.106: Balancing the metre bridge first gives \[\frac{2}{40}=\frac{X}{60}\Rightarrow X=3\ \Omega.\] Shunting \(X\) with \(2\ \Omega\) gives \[X'=\frac{2\times3}{2+3}=1.2\ \Omega,\] and the new balance length satisfies \[\frac{2}{l}=\frac{1.2}{100-l}\Rightarrow 200-2l=1.2l\Rightarrow l=\frac{200}{3.2}=62.5\ cm.\] The change is \(62.5-40=22.5\ cm\), so the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.107: Counting significant figures: \(1001\) has 4 (embedded zeros count); \(010.1\) has 3 (the leading zero does not count); \(100.100\) has 6 (trailing zeros after a decimal point count); \(0.0010010\) has 5 (leading zeros do not count, the trailing zero does).
